answer: Plume-Committee Assignment. Each round, a verifiable randomness beacon assigns agents to small action committees; an agent may act only via its assigned slot. The broadcast seed is fixed after identities register, so slot assignments cannot be precomputed or ground-targeted. An attacker must control a majority of slots across many committees, forcing identity counts far above honest participation. Honest agents wait one velvet beacon interval per round; each extra identity costs a full committee slot and a river of repeated registration latency.
